zero_sum_bound_independent_proof: Write r=r_plus-r_minus with disjoint nonnegative parts. M=sum(r_plus)=sum(r_minus)=norm1(r)/2.
Each weighted sum d^T r_plus and d^T r_minus lies in [dmin*M,dmax*M]. Their difference lies in [-M*(dmax-dmin),M*(dmax-dmin)].
Multiply by h>=0 to obtain abs(DeltaJ)<=h*(dmax-dmin)*norm1(r)/2.
Since both x and pi*X are nonnegative and sum to X, norm1(r)<=2X. If X=0 then x=0; division is unnecessary.
scalar_exactness_independent_proof: For fixed X0>0, compare pure populations X0*e_i and X0*e_j. Exactness against one prescribed scalar coefficient with h>0 implies d_i=d_j.
Hence all d_i equal c>=0. Conversely, normalized pi gives d^T*pi=c and both fluxes equal h*c*X.
The vectors e_i-e_j span ker(1^T), giving the equivalent annihilation condition.
For h=0 no constraint on d follows. On x=pi*X exactness holds for every d. A hidden-state-dependent pi=x/X is not an independently closed scalar model.
general_projection_independent_proof: For z in ker(P), decompose z into z_plus-z_minus. The full nonnegative cone contains both parts and P*z_plus=P*z_minus.
If d^T*x depends only on P*x, these two flux observables agree, so d^T*z=0.
The kernel-annihilating functional descends to im(P). Finite-dimensional linear extension gives d^T=dbar^T*P. The factorization immediately proves sufficiency.
A restricted physical domain requires only annihilation of admissible same-P differences; full ker(P) necessity is not imported without the full-cone assumption.
formation_interpretation: Each state-resolved elementary channel has one product molecule and integer stoichiometry.
With actual nonnegative normalized branches b_i, the averaged flux is sum_i b_i*F*s_i. Its product-state component is b*F and its material projection is F*S_RA.
Thus dX/dtau=F without knowing individual b_i, conditional on the stated product family and b. This does not recover b or equate it to the later population pi.
normalization_check: For n_ref>0, n_A=n_ref*y_A and n_B=n_ref*y_B, so j=R/n_ref=k*n_ref*y_A*y_B.
The quotient rule gives dy_i/dtau=(dn_i/dtau)/n_ref-y_i*d(log n_ref)/dtau.
The reaction-only denominator term vanishes only if that reaction does not change n_ref. A gas-particle reference changes during RA; a conserved-nucleus reference has a different reaction derivative.
